article_units.name: Fitness and Body Systems
article_units.subtitle: Applied anatomy and physiology, movement analysis, physical training and using data in sport.

lessons.title: The Skeleton: Functions and Structure
lessons.description: Bones of the skeleton, classification by shape and the six functions of the skeleton applied to sport.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L1 is ~95% transferable. Edexcel additionally requires bone CLASSIFICATION by shape (long, short, flat, irregular) with sporting application — add a paragraph and 2 flashcards. Keep AQA's bone list + functions framing. Re-spec to 1.1.1/1.1.2/1.1.3.

lessons.title: Joints, Ligaments and Tendons
lessons.description: Types of synovial joint, the movements they allow and how ligaments and tendons enable safe movement.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Combine AQA's joint structure detail with Edexcel-required 4 joint TYPES (pivot, hinge, condyloid, ball-and-socket) and worked sporting examples (atlas/axis for tennis head-turn, knee hinge in kicking, wrist condyloid in basketball shot, shoulder ball-and-socket in swimming). AQA covered hinge and ball-and-socket only — extend with pivot + condyloid.

lessons.title: Muscle Types and Major Muscles
lessons.description: Voluntary, involuntary and cardiac muscle, and the location and role of the major skeletal muscles.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L2 mixed muscles with antagonistic pairs and contractions. Edexcel splits these. This lesson covers muscle TYPES (voluntary/involuntary/cardiac — not in AQA L2) and major muscle locations only. Antagonistic pairs and contractions move to L4. Add involuntary + cardiac muscle paragraphs from scratch (fresh fragment); reuse AQA's muscle-location content.

lessons.title: Antagonistic Pairs and Muscle Fibre Types
lessons.description: Agonist and antagonist roles in sporting actions and how slow and fast twitch fibres suit different activities.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Reuse AQA's antagonistic-pair content. Edexcel uniquely requires three fibre types (Type I, IIa, IIx) with sporting matches — AQA does not teach IIa/IIx explicitly. Add a fresh section on fibre type characteristics and how marathon runners vs sprinters differ. Contraction types (isotonic/isometric) move to L5 because Edexcel groups them with movement analysis.

lessons.title: The Cardiovascular System and Exercise
lessons.description: Heart structure, the pathway of blood and how the cardiovascular system responds to physical activity.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L4 transfers ~90%. Edexcel additionally requires functions of red/white blood cells, platelets and plasma — add a short paragraph. Keep AQA's heart-chamber walkthrough, vasoconstriction/vasodilation framing and CO = SV x HR equation.

lessons.title: The Respiratory System and Gas Exchange
lessons.description: The pathway of air, breathing mechanics and how gas exchange in the alveoli supports activity.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L5 is ~95% transferable. Edexcel adds explicit composition of inhaled vs exhaled air (% O2 and CO2) and tidal volume CHANGE during exercise — both already implicit in AQA's content; surface these as named figures. Vital capacity is named in Edexcel — keep prominent.

lessons.title: Aerobic and Anaerobic Exercise
lessons.description: Word equations for energy release, fuel use and how exercise intensity determines the energy system used.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Reuse AQA's word equations and aerobic/anaerobic justification framing. Edexcel uniquely names FATS as a fuel for aerobic activity (AQA covered glucose only). Add a short paragraph on fat as an endurance fuel. EPOC and recovery methods move to L8 to align with Edexcel's short-term/long-term split.

lessons.title: Short-Term Effects of Exercise
lessons.description: How heart rate, breathing rate, depth and lactate levels change during physical activity.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L7 mixed short- and long-term effects in one lesson. Edexcel splits these across spec sections 1.4.1-1.4.4 (short-term) and 1.4.5-1.4.6 (long-term). Take the short-term half of AQA L7, expand with Edexcel-required cardiovascular-respiratory cooperation under exercise stress.

lessons.title: Long-Term Effects of Training
lessons.description: Adaptations to the body systems from sustained training, including hypertrophy and resting heart rate changes.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Take the long-term half of AQA L7. Edexcel expects sport-specific application (which adaptations matter to a marathon runner vs a powerlifter) — add a worked comparison. Bradycardia and cardiac hypertrophy carry across cleanly.

lessons.title: Lever Systems and Mechanical Advantage
lessons.description: First, second and third class levers in sport and the role of mechanical advantage and disadvantage.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L8 transfers ~95%. Keep LFE order memory aid (1st = F middle, 2nd = L middle, 3rd = E middle). Edexcel uses identical sporting examples (head nod = 1st class, calf raise = 2nd, bicep curl = 3rd). Mechanical advantage/disadvantage is the same.

lessons.title: Planes and Axes of Movement
lessons.description: Sagittal, frontal and transverse planes and the axes that paired movements rotate about in sport.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L9 transfers ~95%. Edexcel names axis as 'vertical' rather than AQA's 'longitudinal' — use vertical in this build. Keep the somersault/cartwheel/pirouette mnemonics. Movement pairings (sagittal-frontal, frontal-sagittal, transverse-vertical) are identical.

lessons.title: Health, Fitness and Components of Fitness
lessons.description: Definitions of health, fitness, exercise and performance and the ten components needed for sport.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L10 transfers ~90%. Edexcel uniquely defines EXERCISE and PERFORMANCE as terms (AQA only defines health and fitness) — add definitions. Edexcel includes body composition as a component of fitness. Components otherwise identical.

lessons.title: Fitness Tests and Interpreting Results
lessons.description: Standard fitness tests, their purpose, and how to compare test results against normative data.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L11 transfers ~85%. Edexcel uniquely lists Cooper 12-minute run (AQA used only MSFT for CV endurance). Edexcel emphasises comparison with NORMATIVE DATA tables — add a worked example showing a student score being graded against age/gender norms. Tests, validity and reliability all transfer.

lessons.title: Principles of Training and Programme Design
lessons.description: Individual needs, specificity, progressive overload, FITT and how training programmes are tailored to goals.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L12 transfers ~90%. Edexcel uses individual needs + specificity + progressive overload + FITT — slightly different acronym from AQA's SPORT, but contents overlap. Reframe around 'individual needs first' which is the Edexcel emphasis. Add rest/recovery and overtraining as explicit Edexcel content.

lessons.title: Methods of Training and Their Effects
lessons.description: Continuous, fartlek, interval, circuit, weight and plyometric training and the components of fitness each develops.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L13 transfers cleanly. Edexcel groups training methods with their long-term aerobic and anaerobic effects (3.4.1-3.4.4), so add a 'matching method to adaptation' table at end of lesson — e.g. continuous training -> cardiac hypertrophy, plyometric -> fast-twitch recruitment.

lessons.title: Injury Prevention, PARQ, RICE and PEDs
lessons.description: Pre-screening readiness, common injuries, the RICE recovery protocol and the role of performance-enhancing drugs.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Mash up AQA L14 (optimising training) + AQA L15 (warm up/cool down) + a fragment of AQA L12 (Socio unit, PEDs). Edexcel uniquely combines all of these under spec section 3.5/3.6 (injury prevention + warm-up). PARQ and RICE are Edexcel-named acronyms — make these explicit. PEDs sit in Component 1 for Edexcel (not Paper 2 like AQA), so the categories are needed here.

lessons.title: Using Data in Physical Activity and Sport
lessons.description: Qualitative and quantitative data, presenting it in tables and graphs, and interpreting against normative data.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L16 covers the same ground but Edexcel weights data-analysis higher (Topic 4 is embedded in EVERY component). Add specifically: comparing results to NORMATIVE DATA and EVALUATING (concluding with judgement). Edexcel's Calculate command word also requires fitness-data computation — include a worked CO = SV × HR question.

article_units.name: Health and Performance
article_units.subtitle: Health and wellbeing, sport psychology and the socio-cultural impact of physical activity and sport.

lessons.title: Physical, Emotional and Social Wellbeing
lessons.description: How participation in sport supports physical health, mental health and social health, and reduces health risks.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L14 (Socio) transfers cleanly. Edexcel uses 'emotional' rather than AQA's 'mental' health — change terminology consistently. Add the negative side: how poor fitness or over-training harms each of the three wellbeing domains (Edexcel 1.1.4 specifically asks for positive AND negative impacts).

lessons.title: Lifestyle Choices and Sedentary Living
lessons.description: Diet, sleep, alcohol and smoking, and the long-term health consequences of a sedentary lifestyle.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L15 (Socio) covered sedentary lifestyle, obesity and somatotypes together. Edexcel SPLITS these — somatotypes are NOT in Edexcel 1PE0 spec (omit entirely). Add Edexcel-required lifestyle factors (work/rest/sleep balance, alcohol, nicotine, recreational drug effects) which AQA bundled elsewhere.

lessons.title: Diet, Nutrition and Hydration
lessons.description: Macronutrients, micronutrients, energy balance and how dehydration affects sporting performance.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L16 (Socio) transfers ~85%. Edexcel uniquely requires CARBOHYDRATE LOADING for endurance and PROTEIN TIMING for power athletes — add named worked examples (marathon runner pre-race carb load, sprinter post-session protein within 30 minutes). Optimum weight factors (sex, height, bone structure, muscle girth) are Edexcel-named — keep prominent.

lessons.title: Classification of Skills and Practice Structures
lessons.description: Basic/complex, open/closed and high/low organisation continua, and matching practice to skill type.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L1 (Socio) covered open/closed, basic/complex and self-paced/externally-paced. Edexcel REPLACES the third continuum with high-organisation/low-organisation (a different distinction). Drop self-paced/externally-paced framing; add organisation continuum. Also fresh: practice STRUCTURES (massed, distributed, fixed, variable) — these are not in AQA. Add a fresh-from-spec section.

lessons.title: Goal Setting and SMART Targets
lessons.description: How goal setting motivates performers and the SMART principles for writing effective sporting targets.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L2 (Socio) transfers ~95%. AQA uses SMART with 'accepted' for A; Edexcel uses 'achievable' for A — change the A definition. Add Edexcel-specific 'reviewing targets' content (the cyclical nature of goal setting).

lessons.title: Guidance and Feedback in Sport
lessons.description: Visual, verbal, manual and mechanical guidance and the four types of feedback used to improve performance.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Combine AQA L4 (guidance) and L5 (feedback). AQA used 'knowledge of results' and 'knowledge of performance' feedback types; Edexcel uses CONCURRENT and TERMINAL instead. Replace those two AQA terms with Edexcel's — keep intrinsic/extrinsic which are common. Drop AQA's KR/KP from the active vocabulary.

lessons.title: Mental Preparation for Performance
lessons.description: Mental rehearsal, imagery and arousal control techniques that prepare an athlete for competition.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L6 (Socio) covered arousal AND the inverted-U theory in depth. Edexcel does NOT require the inverted-U theory — only mental preparation techniques. Drop inverted-U; refocus on mental rehearsal, imagery, deep breathing, positive self-talk and the warm-up's mental preparation role. AQA's inverted-U content can flag a 'fresh' subsection.

lessons.title: Engagement Patterns in Sport
lessons.description: How gender, age, socio-economic group, ethnicity and disability shape participation rates in sport.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L8 (Socio) transfers ~90%. Edexcel groups gender/age/socio-economic/ethnicity/disability (drops AQA's religion/family/culture). Edexcel uniquely requires INTERPRETATION OF GRAPHICAL DATA on participation trends as part of this spec section — build in a worked chart-reading example with original Sport England-style data.

lessons.title: Commercialisation, Sponsorship and the Media
lessons.description: The golden triangle of sport, sponsorship and media, and the impacts on sponsors, sports, performers and spectators.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L9 (Socio) transfers cleanly. Edexcel uniquely structures advantages/disadvantages by FOUR named stakeholders: sponsor, sport, player/performer, spectator. Restructure into a 4-stakeholder table. Edexcel also requires interpreting graphical data on commercialisation trends — add original example chart.

lessons.title: Ethical Behaviour and Deviance in Sport
lessons.description: Sportsmanship, gamesmanship and the reasons for and consequences of deviance at elite level.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L11 covered etiquette, sportsmanship, gamesmanship and the contract to compete. Edexcel drops etiquette and contract-to-compete and adds DEVIANCE AT ELITE LEVEL (match-fixing, bribery, violence, doping). Reframe to sportsmanship vs gamesmanship vs deviance — three tiers. Need a fresh paragraph on deviance with consequences.

lessons.title: Performance Enhancing Drugs (Recap and Application)
lessons.description: Categories of PEDs, the reasons performers use them, and the consequences for performer, sport and integrity.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L12 (Socio) covered PEDs in depth. Edexcel places PEDs primarily in Component 1 (Physical Training 3.5.5) but they recur in Component 2 deviance. Treat this lesson as an APPLICATION revisit: focus on consequences for performer/sport/integrity rather than re-teaching the categories. Reference the earlier Component 1 lesson for the chemistry.

lessons.title: Interpreting Data on Health and Participation
lessons.description: Reading tables, bar charts, line graphs and pie charts that describe health, fitness and participation trends.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L17 covered the same skill set but Edexcel weights data interpretation higher in Component 2 (Topic 4 embedded throughout). Use Health/Wellbeing scenarios for this lesson: obesity trends, gender participation gaps, age-related decline curves. Build original example data — never reproduce real Sport England figures.

lessons.title: Revision Synthesis: Component 2 Synoptic Practice
lessons.description: Bringing together health, sport psychology and socio-cultural content to tackle 9-mark extended response questions.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Fresh build. AQA has no equivalent — Edexcel's Component 2 has a SINGLE 9-mark extended response question linking sport psychology AND socio-cultural influences (per spec p.16). Students need synthesis practice. This lesson teaches the 9-mark structure: balanced argument, sporting application, conclusion. Include 3 worked answer plans and 2 practice 9-mark questions linking psychology + socio-cultural.

unique_to_source.lesson: 10 — Health, Fitness and Components of Fitness
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Edexcel keeps the same components but body composition is named explicitly as a component — merged into Edexcel L12.
Edexcel 1PE0 does not include an information-processing model in its sport psychology topic — input/decision/output is not specified content.
Inverted-U arousal theory is not in the Edexcel 1PE0 spec. Mental preparation techniques are covered in Edexcel L7 but without the inverted-U graph.
Personality types (introvert/extrovert), aggression and intrinsic/extrinsic motivation are not in Edexcel 1PE0's sport psychology topic.
Technology in sport is not a standalone Edexcel topic — touched implicitly under commercialisation but not assessed directly.
Hooliganism and spectator strategies are not in Edexcel 1PE0 spec content.

unique_to_source.lesson: 15 — Sedentary Lifestyle, Obesity and Somatotypes (somatotype portion)
unique_to_source.why_not_in_target: Somatotypes (ectomorph/mesomorph/endomorph) are not in the Edexcel 1PE0 spec. Sedentary lifestyle is covered in Edexcel L2.

unique_to_target.lesson: 16 — Injury Prevention, PARQ, RICE and PEDs
unique_to_target.why_no_source_match: Edexcel uniquely bundles PARQ pre-screening, the RICE protocol and PED categories under Physical Training (3.5). AQA spreads these across multiple lessons; PEDs sat in the Socio unit.
Edexcel's Component 2 9-mark extended response uniquely synthesises sport psychology and socio-cultural content in a single question. Students need a dedicated lesson on the synoptic structure.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students label a sport 'aerobic' or 'anaerobic' without anchoring to intensity and duration. The Edexcel mark scheme expects justified reasoning ('100m sprint, ~10s at maximal intensity, insufficient oxygen reaching working muscles -> anaerobic'). Generic 'because it's short' answers lose marks.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Physical Education teacher support (https://qualifications.pearson.com/en/qualifications/edexcel-gcses/physical-education-2016.html)

common_misconceptions.topic: Lever diagrams — load, fulcrum, effort order
common_misconceptions.misconception: Students mis-order LFE when drawing or labelling levers, especially the third-class lever (effort between fulcrum and load — applies to the bicep curl). Mark schemes require the correct visual ordering on labelled diagrams. The 'F-L-E / L-F-E / E-F-L is wrong' framing fails because Edexcel insists on the middle component identifying the class (1st = F middle, 2nd = L middle, 3rd = E middle).

Students confuse the open-closed continuum with basic-complex or low-organisation/high-organisation. Edexcel uses THREE separate continua (basic/complex, open/closed, low-org/high-org) — they are not synonymous. Open = environment changes (football pass under pressure); complex = many decisions/moving parts (gymnastics routine); high-org = subroutines hard to separate (golf swing). A skill can be high on one continuum and low on another.

Students write SMART targets that are not actually measurable or time-bound ('get better at football this term'). Mark schemes credit only targets that are simultaneously specific (named skill), measurable (number/percentage), achievable, realistic (relative to current ability) and time-bound (a deadline). Edexcel uses 'achievable' for A, not 'accepted'.

Students treat the 9-mark question as a description task — they list facts about both topics but don't link, evaluate or apply to sporting context. Edexcel's Evaluate command word requires a supported judgement; the rubric rewards (a) range, (b) balance (advantages and disadvantages), (c) sporting application throughout, (d) conclusion. One-sided answers cap at level 1.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson Edexcel 1PE0 specification Appendix 6 Command Word Taxonomy (https://qualifications.pearson.com/en/qualifications/edexcel-gcses/physical-education-2016.html)

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students extract a single number from a graph without saying what it shows or comparing it. Edexcel mark schemes for Interpret Data questions credit: (1) quote a figure with units, (2) make a comparison or trend statement, (3) explain the sporting implication. Naming the trend without a number, or quoting a number without context, both lose a mark.

student_errors_by_question_type.9 marks — Evaluate: Edexcel's single 9-mark question on Component 2 expects synthesis of sport psychology AND socio-cultural content. Students often answer only one topic. Force a 'For… However…' structure with a sporting example and a conclusion sentence. Mark scheme: level 1 (1-3) = limited, level 2 (4-6) = developed one-sided, level 3 (7-9) = balanced + applied + concluded.
student_errors_by_question_type.6 marks — Assess: Edexcel's Assess command word requires REASONED ARGUMENT to reach a judgement on the relative importance of factors. Students often describe factors without weighing them. Teach: identify the factors, compare them, conclude with a ranking and a reason.
student_errors_by_question_type.6 marks — Analyse: Students list rather than analyse. Each point should be: state the factor, link to performance, give a sporting example. Avoid bullet-point answers; the mark scheme rewards continuous prose with sporting application.
student_errors_by_question_type.4 marks — Discuss: Edexcel's Discuss requires exploring DIFFERENT or CONTRASTING viewpoints (advantages and disadvantages). Single-sided discussions cap at half marks. Teach 'On one hand… on the other…' as scaffolding.
student_errors_by_question_type.3 marks — Explain: Students give the WHAT without the WHY. Edexcel mark schemes for Explain reward 'fact… because… therefore…' chains of reasoning. State the point, give the reason, state the consequence.
student_errors_by_question_type.2 marks — Calculate: Students forget units (bpm, %, ml, seconds) or skip working. Mark schemes typically award 1 for correct working, 1 for the answer with units. CO = SV × HR style calculations are likely in Component 1 — show all three steps.
student_errors_by_question_type.1 mark — Identify: Students give two answers when one is required, hedging. Mark schemes typically take the FIRST answer — extra answers can be ignored or, if contradictory, lose the mark. Teach: pick one, commit.

topic_weighting_notes: Component 1 (Fitness and Body Systems) is 36% of the qualification and 80 marks. Applied anatomy and physiology + Physical training dominate. Section A focuses on Topics 1-2, Section B on Topic 3, Section C is the single extended-response question. Use of data is embedded across all sections.

Component 2 (Health and Performance) is 24% of the qualification and 60 marks. Section A is Topic 1 (health/wellbeing/diet), Section B is Topics 2 and 3 (sport psychology and socio-cultural). Section C is a single 9-mark extended response linking sport psychology AND socio-cultural — a synoptic synthesis. This is unique to Edexcel.

Use of Data (Topic 4) does NOT have its own section in either paper — it is embedded throughout. Every lesson should include at least one Interpret Data, Calculate or original-data flavoured question where the content is amenable. Data fluency is a high-volume mark-earning skill.

Practical NEA (Components 3 and 4) is 30% + 10% of the qualification and is teacher-assessed. This revision platform does not address it. The 30 lessons cover 100% of the assessable theory content (60% of the qualification grade).
current_spec_changes: Specification Issue 5 (September 2024) is the current authoritative document. The only change between Issue 4 and Issue 5 is a typographic correction on the NEA activity list (inline / roller hockey — slash removed). No content additions or removals affect Paper 1 or Paper 2 for the 2026 series. Source: https://qualifications.pearson.com/en/qualifications/edexcel-gcses/physical-education-2016.html
pedagogical_notes: EEF retrieval-practice guidance: real retrieval (free recall, blank-page brain dumps, low-stakes quizzing) outperforms re-reading. Knowledge checks and flashcards in this build must require active recall, not recognition — phrase flashcard questions to elicit a definition rather than a multiple choice. Source: https://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/news/eef-blog-not-another-quiz-refining-retrieval-practice

EEF cognitive science review: dual coding (words paired with imagery) is high-utility but free-tier lessons cannot embed generated diagrams. Where a diagram would clarify (heart chambers, lever systems, planes/axes), the prose must do the imaging work — describe the anatomy precisely AND include a 'sketch this without looking' retrieval prompt. Source: https://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/education-evidence/evidence-reviews/cognitive-science-approaches-in-the-classroom

EEF spaced-practice principle: revisit material across days. Lessons should cross-reference earlier content explicitly (when teaching long-term effects in L9, retrieve the cardiovascular response from L5 and respiratory response from L6). This builds the synoptic understanding that Edexcel's 9-mark question demands. Source: https://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/news/eef-blog-putting-cognitive-science-principles-into-practice

EEF interleaving: mixing related topics in retrieval forces discrimination. Component 2 knowledge checks should mix sport psychology with socio-cultural content — Edexcel rewards this synthesis directly via the 9-mark question. Component 1 should mix anatomy with training. Source: https://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/news/eef-blog-the-abc-of-cognitive-science

Glossary terms: PE is terminology-dense. Aim for at least 6 inline glossary terms per lesson; 8-10 is realistic in anatomy-heavy lessons. Definitions one sentence, reusable across lessons. The Edexcel Appendix 5 glossary of key terms is a useful checklist (no need to copy verbatim — paraphrase).

Edexcel command words: Edexcel uses Assess, Analyse, Calculate, Classify, Complete, Define, Describe, Discuss, Examine, Explain, Evaluate, Give, Identify, Justify, Label, Predict, Select, State. Practice questions must match these command words. Avoid AQA's 'Analyse' phrasing when the Edexcel equivalent is 'Assess' or 'Examine'.

Data interpretation: Edexcel Topic 4 is embedded across BOTH papers. Generate original fictional data tables and graph descriptions — never reproduce real Sport England, NHS or Edexcel figures. Use realistic numbers (e.g. 'Sarah's heart rate during a 30-minute run: rest 70 bpm, peak 165 bpm, recovery 90 bpm at 5 min'). Include at least one Interpret Data or Calculate question per lesson where the content is amenable.

Mark scheme rubric: StudyVault uses Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging on 6- and 9-mark levels-based questions. NEVER use 'Level 1/2/3', 'Nothing worthy of credit' or 'Award X marks for Y' (the validator bans the 'Award N marks for' pattern). Phrase mark allocations as '1 mark for X; 1 mark for Y' or 'Up to 3 marks: identification (1), reasoning (1), application (1)'.

Plain-text fields (description, practice_questions[].text/.type/.marks, knowledge_checks[].q, flashcard_questions[].q/.a, glossary_terms[].term/.definition) MUST use plain unicode (apostrophes, en-dashes, em-dashes typed directly). NEVER use HTML entities such as ’, &, – in these fields — entities are only allowed inside content_html, exam_tip_html, conclusion_html.

Copyright: do not include spec codes (1PE0), component codes (1PE0/01, 1PE0/02), section labels, or Edexcel trademark question stems verbatim. Do not reproduce Edexcel mark scheme phrasing. Build generic GCSE-level questions with our 13 registered command-word types.

Knowledge check shape: use `correct: <int>` (integer index) plus `options: [string, string, ...]` — NEVER write `answers: [...]` (text-array shape). The quick-quiz player breaks silently on the wrong shape. (Validator catches it pre-insert but content agents have hallucinated this before.)

gaps: Components 3 and 4 (Practical Performance and Personal Exercise Programme — 40% of the qualification combined) are teacher-assessed and not addressed by this revision platform. Students are pointed to their school's PE department for activity assessment and the PEP coursework. The 30 lessons in this plan cover 100% of the assessable theory content for Component 1 and Component 2 (60% of the qualification).

Spec section 1.1.10 (fast vs slow twitch fibre types) is covered in Component 1 L4. Edexcel uniquely splits fibres into Type I, IIa and IIx. Our lesson teaches all three; mark schemes accept 'fast twitch' and 'slow twitch' alone for 1-mark answers but the full three-type detail is needed for 3-mark+ questions.

Spec section 3.4 (long-term training effects) is split between L9 (general body adaptations) and L15 (matching methods to adaptations). This avoids a single overloaded lesson but means content agents must cross-reference both lessons.
